# Example transcript: running s09.
#
# This is an ILLUSTRATIVE run, not a byte-exact fixture. The LINT-mode output
# (the report the loop would reflect back) is deterministic for a given file and
# is essentially what the tests pin. The RUN-mode behaviour depends on a live
# LLM, so for that part what matters is the SHAPE: a broken edit gets caught,
# fed back, and fixed within the reflection cap.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. LINT mode (no network, no API key): run just the Linter over a broken Go
#    file and print exactly what the loop would hand back to the model. The
#    built-in checker is `gofmt -l -e`.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ cat broken.go
package main

func main() {
    x :=
}

$ go run . -lint broken.go
# Fix any errors below, if possible.

## Running: gofmt broken.go

broken.go:4:9: expected operand, found '}'

# --- stderr ---
[s09] ^ in RUN mode this exact text becomes a synthetic user message,
      handed back to the model so it can fix the code.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LINT a clean file: nothing to reflect, exit 0.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -lint provider.go
lint clean: nothing to reflect

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. RUN mode: ask the model to edit a file. The whole-file Coder writes the
#    reply; the Linter checks it; a clean result stops after the first pass.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
$ go run . -v -file calc.go -instruction "add a Divide(a, b int) int function"

# --- stderr (the -v trace) ---
[s09] provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-4-6 file=calc.go max-reflections=3
[s09] clean on the first try — no reflection needed.

# --- stdout ---
applied 1 edit(s) to calc.go across 1 pass(es)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. RUN mode where the model's first edit does NOT compile. The reflection
#    loop catches it, feeds the gofmt error back, and the model fixes it on the
#    second pass. The interesting line is "converged after 1 reflection(s)".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -v -file calc.go -instruction "add a function with a deliberate typo, then fix it"

# --- stderr ---
[s09] provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-4-6 file=calc.go max-reflections=3
[s09] converged after 1 reflection(s) — lint is now clean.

# --- stdout ---
applied 2 edit(s) to calc.go across 2 pass(es)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. If the model never converges, the loop stops at the cap rather than
#    looping forever (here -max-reflections 2). The still-broken lint report is
#    printed so a human can take over.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -file calc.go -instruction "..." -max-reflections 2
[s09] stopped after 2 reflection(s): cap reached, still not clean:
# Fix any errors below, if possible.

## Running: gofmt calc.go

calc.go:7:1: expected declaration, found '}'
applied 3 edit(s) to calc.go across 3 pass(es)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. The deterministic tests (these DO run in CI, no network):
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go test ./...
ok  	learn-aider/s09	0.5s
